headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: Open Interpreter and Roo Code can both write, execute, and modify shared workspace state by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read/write the whole filesystem and uses clipboard/stdin-stdout; Roo Code can read/write VS Code workspace files and also use MCP. A shared filesystem bridge exists, so attacker-controlled content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. This is not provably blocked, but it is not a raw shared-channel default like MCP-to-MCP.
conditions: IF either agent consumes files produced by the other as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected through a shared workspace or copied text, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic execution of file-derived instructions.
Keep the agents on separate directories/workspaces.
Require human review before one agent reads the other's outputs.
Add provenance tags to generated files.
Use read-only handoff files for inter-agent communication.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read broad local files and write outputs, and Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine while Roo Code reads workspace files and can call external APIs/MCP. If sensitive data is present in the shared filesystem, either agent can expose it through its configured model/API path. The blast radius includes secrets and source code, so this is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared filesystem, either agent can ingest them.
IF Roo Code is configured with an external model API or MCP server, workspace contents may leave the machine.
mitigations: Separate sensitive files from the shared workspace.
Use local-only models for both agents.
Remove API keys from directories either agent can read.
Restrict Roo Code MCP servers to trusted local endpoints.
Run each agent under a different OS user.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, and git-state modification, and both share state via filesystem. Concurrent edits to the same workspace or repo can race and corrupt files or git history. Because both can act on the same mutable resources without locking, the conflict pathway is strong and default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or git repository, write conflicts can occur.
IF either agent runs package installs while the other edits the same workspace, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git branches per agent.
Enable file locking or a single-writer workflow.
Review diffs before any commit.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate code and filesystem changes, and Roo Code can act on workspace content with shell and browser tools. If Roo Code treats Open Interpreter's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into executed commands, commits, or browser actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so downstream amplification is plausible by default.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes Open Interpreter output without verification, incorrect instructions can be executed.
IF Open Interpreter writes code or plans into the workspace, Roo Code may operationalize them.
mitigations: Require a verification step before execution.
Mark AI-generated files as untrusted.
Use a separate review-only workspace.
Disable auto-run modes.
Limit browser or shell actions to approved commands.

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter can touch anything reachable on the local machine, while Roo Code reads workspace files and may send them to configured model APIs or MCP servers. If regulated data such as EU PII or secrets is stored in those files, the pair can create residency or retention mismatches. The profiles do not specify a formal DPA or certification gap, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files accessible to both agents, compliance obligations apply.
IF Roo Code is configured to send workspace content to a third-party API, residency/retention controls must be checked.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared workspaces.
Use approved regional model endpoints only.
Rotate or remove secrets before shared use.
Document retention settings for both tools.
Run compliance-sensitive tasks in a separate environment.
